html:
A nominally independent state in the Russian Far East, from Lake Baikal to the Pacific, set up by the Bolsheviks in 1920 and folded into Soviet Russia in 1922. The map shows the region under this label in 1920 and 1930.

During the Russian Civil War, Japanese troops held Vladivostok and much of the coast as part of the Allied Siberian intervention. Lenin's government did not want open war with Japan, so it created a buffer state with its own army and a democratic face, first at Verkhneudinsk and then at Chita. Its army defeated the last White forces, and when the Japanese withdrew in October 1922 it took Vladivostok. A month later it voted to join Soviet Russia.

By 1930 the area was the Far Eastern Krai, a region of the Soviet Union tied to the west by the Trans-Siberian Railway. The 1930 label keeps the old name for what was by then simply the Soviet Far East.
